$comment: The machine-readable answer to 'what is happening now?'. It is not a historical database: completed stages are ids only, and the narrative for anything closed lives in Git. docs/ROADMAP.md sequences; this file states.
currentStage: Phase 4.4 — high-value application capabilities, opened on the dependency that is already proven rather than on the whole 4.3 table
blockedBy: Nothing blocks the active stage. Phase 4.4 was opened on 2026-08-28 and the transition is recorded here rather than assumed, because a stage that opens itself is not a decision. The rule is the same one used to defer 4D: stage progression is about the dependencies the NEXT real work needs, not about every optional parity feature being finished. Three things had to be true and each was measured. (1) Application-renderer metadata correctness is materially improved and proved on BUILT output - see phase-4-3-application-renderer-ships-no-crawlable-metadata, and docs/RENDERER_SELECTION.md for the route-crawlability decision that travels with it. (2) Read-only brownfield adoption has real acceptance on a mature outside repository with zero mutations, not on a fixture written to be found. (3) No 4.3 capability that remains absent is a prerequisite for application work: CMS/content collections, localisation and Figma import are each genuinely unbuilt, each is recorded in deferredCapabilities as planned and unproven, and NONE of them is depended on by auth, tenancy, database security or application state. They are not complete and are not claimed to be. Phase 4D visual excellence also remains FAILED and unpaid at the unchanged 8.5 threshold, deferred rather than discharged, with docs/PHASE_4D_VISUAL_DEBT.md as the durable record and its revival conditions unchanged by this transition. The one genuine input blocker in the corpus lane is owner-only and named in phase-4-3-second-corpus-business: it is a rights approval, not code, and it stops no engineering.
outstandingProductGates: phase-4-4-first-application-slice: FIRST SLICE DELIVERED 2026-08-28, and Phase 4.4 is NOT complete. A generated B2B SaaS application now has organisation-owned domain records: `recipes/records` contributes a `records` table with a real foreign key to `public.organisations`, per-organisation unique references, role-differentiated RLS built on the existing `app_private.has_org_role`, and ONE bounded privileged operation - `public.set_record_archived`, a narrow security definer function rather than a blanket RLS bypass, because the `admin` recipe is client-side `app_metadata` and says of itself that UI gating is not authorization. Proved on a real PostgreSQL: tooling/supabase-rls-acceptance.sql grew from 18 to 44 assertions over the SAME six deterministic identities and two organisations it already had, covering same-tenant read and write, cross-tenant read/update/delete refusal, organisation-id forgery, authorship forgery, anonymous refusal, viewer-vs-member-vs-owner distinction, and the archive boundary in both directions. PROOF OF PROOF: tooling/records-mutation-check.sh breaks six safeguards in turn against the generated schema and requires the suite to fail each time - all six are killed. It found two safeguards that had NO test behind them (the UPDATE policy's own tenant predicate, which the SELECT policy was masking, and the privileged column, whose assertion never actually tried to write it) and one defect in itself (a mutation that raised aborted the transaction, emitted no `not ok`, and was misread as a pass). It also found a REAL security defect: a Supabase database ships `alter default privileges ... grant all on tables to authenticated`, so the column-level `grant update (...)` pattern used here and in the organisations/profiles recipes does NOT restrict anything - the narrower grant adds, it does not subtract. `archived_at` is therefore defended by a trigger, not by a withheld grant. THE SAME QUESTION IS OPEN FOR THE EXISTING RECIPES: organisations' `grant update (name, slug)` and profiles' `grant update (display_name, avatar_url, updated_at)` are likely not restrictive either. Not fixed here because it is not this capability's defect to fix, and it needs its own acceptance. STILL OPEN in 4.4: transactional email, uploads, notifications, webhooks, jobs and billing are all untouched, and the browser journey is CI-verified rather than locally verified because the Supabase CLI cannot drive podman on this host.

phase-4-3-capability-closure: Phase 4.3 is the active stage and NOTHING in it may be claimed because a plan names it. The stage-placement table in docs/PLATFORM_PARITY_PROGRAMME.md §13 lists CMS/content collections, localisation, design/Figma import, existing-repository adoption, mature source upload and the deterministic SEO/AEO scanner at this stage. CLOSED 2026-08-28: the SEO/AEO scanner. config/gate-producers.json listed seo-aeo-scanner under `unregistered` - a check gates.seo declares and no producer answered - so the seo gate had never been measured on any build. tooling/lib/seo-aeo.mjs now answers it from the BUILT DOCUMENTS rather than the composition, because what a renderer emits is a separate fact from what a composer decided and only the first is what a crawler receives. STILL ABSENT and genuinely unbuilt rather than partly built: no localisation beyond one NFR schema field, no content collections beyond a questionnaire, no Figma import of any kind, and no brownfield/existing-repository reader. CLOSED 2026-08-28 for its READ-ONLY half: existing-repository adoption now has a first proven slice. tooling/lib/brownfield-profile.mjs reads a repository and describes its identity, workspace, stack, architecture, data/backend, testing, deployment and (shallowly) design system, and every field is demonstrated / inferred / unproven / not-applicable with the evidence behind it. Read-only is ENFORCED rather than promised: brownfield-evidence.mjs runs a closed list of git subcommands with --no-optional-locks, because an ordinary `git status` rewrites .git/index; symlinks are not followed, so another project cannot be reported as this one; and the CLI refuses an --out inside the profiled repository. Proved on a real mature repository, not a fixture - the adopted repository is identified in examples/brownfield/, which is outside the contamination guard's scope for exactly this reason, and no adopted product's name belongs in factory configuration. 3263 files read in 89ms, ZERO mutations with every path/size/mtime in the working tree AND in .git fingerprinted before and after. Its numbers were then checked by hand against source and agree exactly - 218 migrations, 188 database tests, 67 CI workflows, 69 SQL files declaring RLS or a policy, 55 e2e files, 719 unit files, 3 Supabase edge functions. It correctly REFUSED four things: route locations (the subject routes through react-router inside its root App component and has no pages/ directory, so there was nothing to find and inventing routes would have been the first fabrication), a typecheck command that does not exist, auth as anything stronger than `a library is a dependency`, and design-system assimilation - the subject HAS a src/design-system/ directory, and a directory name is not evidence of a design system. The mature repository also found a defect in the profiler itself, which is what it is for: the unit/e2e split matched `e2e` anywhere in a path and case-sensitively, so it excluded tests/scripts/e2eProjectGating.test.ts while keeping five sibling *E2E.test.ts files; it now matches a path segment. examples/brownfield/ holds the frozen baseline and the verification table. STILL ABSENT and deliberately so: no classification (keep/refactor/redesign/replace/remove/add is diagnosis, and diagnosing from a first read is how `replace` comes to mean `the factory prefers a different framework`), no deployed-URL evidence, no execution of any project script, and no design-system assimilation (§5.2). Mutation has NOT been earned by this slice. Do not implement the rest of the table merely because it is listed; implement the capability that has a real consumer.

professional-output-independent-verdict: the one outstanding row in docs/VISUAL_EXCELLENCE.md §9. It is the same gate three times over, because a candidate set, a static rendering and any bespoke presentation each need a reviewer who did not produce the work. All three have now HAD an independent reviewer and none of them passed, so what is outstanding is the quality, not the reviewer. The measured results and the reason they are deferred rather than discharged are in deferredCapabilities and docs/PHASE_4D_VISUAL_DEBT.md. This row may not be marked satisfied by any claim of visual maturity while that debt is unpaid.

evidence-must-depict-what-ships: CLOSED 2026-08-28. The missing fact was never in the picture: it was which artifact was serving, and no assertion about a screenshot could have reached it. RenderedEvidence now requires `renderingSource` - server mode, the artifact served, a hash over every path and byte that artifact contains, and whether it depicts what ships - and it is inside setHash, so a set cannot have its provenance rewritten without its identity changing. buildEvidenceSet REFUSES to mint a set without it: a default would be a guess, and one of the two available guesses is the defect. tooling/lib/rendering-source.mjs owns the question; the review packet lists every refusal in `missing`, which is what makes a run un-validatable, and REVIEW.md states what was captured against above the pictures. Three planted failures prove it: a dev-only marker (refused as a development capture, and shown to change the artifact hash so it cannot hide in one), capturing build A while claiming build B (refused on hash mismatch), and captures reused across a rebuild (refused, `no longer here`). Absence is a refusal too - evidence from before this field existed cannot say what it photographed, and `we do not know` must never be read as `the built artifact`. Ordinary cleanup is NOT tampering: a candidate workspace removed after its set is decided leaves the recorded hash standing and re-verification simply unavailable, because calling that tampering would train people to ignore the check. The compliant path exists rather than only the refusal: serveCandidateBuild is renamed serveBuiltArtifact and captureRenderedEvidence(id, { against: 'built-artifact' }) serves the project's own verified dist, so the ordinary project lane can produce evidence a review may treat as a claim about what ships. The candidate lane already served built output and now says so. The preview lane still photographs the operator's dev server, which is correct for iterating and is now recorded as `development` rather than being silently promotable. Original finding, kept: the general form of a defect that already cost one paid review, and a deterministic-quality gate rather than a visual one - the specific instance was a factory-meta strip rendered under import.meta.env.DEV, photographed and correctly reported by the static-renderer critic as exposed generator metadata in the public footer. Same family as the route-capture defect in #163: the evidence did not depict the product.

nbm-source-pack-ceiling: the frozen nbm case may not be able to reach the 8.5 bar without fabricating facts, and that is a corpus finding rather than a factory defect. Both independent reviews ask for the same missing material - project experience, credentials, qualifications, sectors, team information, client outcomes, process - and buildContract.explicitlyExcluded forbids exactly that: named client or project case studies, republished photographs, and any performance, client, award, accreditation or experience claim no approved source supports. The approved pack is a company name, one registry sentence, four service names with no descriptions, two location names with no detail, one phone number and one address; entities is empty. A typography and layout led direction has a ceiling on that much content and no art direction raises it. Decide deliberately whether the bar is proved on a richer business, whether the owner can approve more nbm material, or whether the bar is wrong for a business this thinly evidenced. Do not close the gap by inventing proof. Measured on the 2026-08-28 rerun: the factory itself now quantifies part of this. The candidate generator REFUSED the immersive-lead direction outright - 'imagery-not-available ... No photographs were supplied at all, so the direction has to carry the page with type and layout' - and assetReadiness records strategy 'typography-led' with supportsImageryLed false. One of three visual directions is unreachable for this business on rights grounds alone, before any judgement of taste. That is a source ceiling the factory measures rather than an opinion about it, and it is the first row of the source-adequacy evidence a second business is needed to turn into a relationship. One row is not a mechanism; do not build a SourceAdequacy subsystem on it. Corrected 2026-08-28: the claim that the approved pack holds no service descriptions and no email address was true of the manifest and false of the sources. Both are present once the declared sources are ingested. The ceiling that survives measurement is proof and imagery - no people, projects, testimonials, accreditations or publishable photographs - not content thinness in general.

phase-4-3-second-corpus-business: OWNER-INPUT BLOCKER, and the only one in this stage. What is missing is not code. The repository holds exactly one genuine business - nbm - and no second approved-intake bundle, ingested pack or durable project exists anywhere in it. A second case is what turns one-project findings into corpus findings, including the component-vocabulary finding in docs/PHASE_4D_VISUAL_DEBT.md, which is revival condition A and cannot be answered from nbm alone. The nearest candidate is already identified and partly specified: MGB Decor (issue #60), a Glasgow painting and decorating business, class marketing-site, with owner-supplied first-party source locations recorded on the issue. It is NOT usable yet. Issue #60 states explicitly that authoritative source locations do not grant republication rights to any photograph, customer image, logo or third-party asset, and no asset-level approval exists in the repository. The precise owner action required is: an explicit, asset-level rights approval plus the owner-supplied facts, frozen in the shape examples/genuine-business/nbm-approved-intake.v1.json already defines. Do not crawl those social profiles and do not infer approval from a URL being public. Never fabricate owner approval. Until that exists this lane waits, and it blocks no other stage.

phase-4-3-corpus-case-metrics: data before dashboard. Each genuine case that is actually run should retain, where the run produces it: factory SHA, frozen input hash, KnowledgePack hash, build success, unsupported claims, meaningful manual edits, interventions, accessibility result, browser failures, responsive result, visual verdict, generic/template finding, journey pass rate, rework loops, model/tool cost and publishable yes/no. nbm is the first calibrated case and its material is frozen: intake, KnowledgePack e7c387bc, 9 sources, 22 facts, source hashes, rights limitations, five independent verdicts and its launch-readiness result are all committed under examples/genuine-business/. Do not regenerate nbm unless a reusable factory change needs regression testing. Do NOT build a Factory Intelligence dashboard on one case.

phase-4-3-application-renderer-ships-no-crawlable-metadata: PARTLY CLOSED 2026-08-28, and what remains is architectural rather than unfixed. The head is now written at GENERATION time. tooling/lib/document-head.mjs composes title, description, og:title/description/type/site_name and the twitter pair from manifest.project; tooling/lib/generator.mjs writes them through a seam the template declares (`document` in template.json); and the scaffold placeholder deliberately stays INSIDE the managed markers, so a substitution that failed to run ships the one title the scanner already refuses rather than failing quietly. Measured on built output rather than argued: tooling/document-metadata-acceptance.mjs installs and builds three generated repositories and reads their dist - a project declaring a site URL (title, description, OG, canonical and og:url all present), the same project without one (canonical and og:url absent, recorded as an advisory limit, never invented), and the defect planted back by restoring the scaffold head (document-title-placeholder and document-description-missing, refused). 13 seconds wall clock, 404MB peak. STILL TRUE AND NOT HIDDEN: the application renderer serves ONE document, so route-metadata-not-crawlable still fires for any composition declaring more than one route, and document-heading-missing fires on every application build because the body is
until React runs. Neither is a head-substitution problem. docs/RENDERER_SELECTION.md records the decision that route-specific crawlable metadata is a RENDERER-SELECTION requirement rather than a universal template feature: public marketing/content sites already default to the static-content renderer, which emits a real document per route; application projects correctly serve one; and no prerendering is added to the neutral Vite template because it would duplicate the static renderer badly. The one uncomfortable shape - a marketing site that enables auth, takes the capability override and loses per-route documents as a side effect - has no project behind it, and is recorded as the revival condition for a hybrid/SSR renderer rather than built speculatively. The original finding, kept because it is the measurement that started this: FOUND by the new SEO/AEO scanner on the factory's own template, and worth separating from taste. templates/react-vite-neutral/files/index.html ships `Generated application` with no meta description, no canonical and no Open Graph tags, and the seo recipe patches metadata in only AFTER hydration - `document.title = project.name`, once, at project level, never per route. The template is a plain Vite SPA with no prerendering, so every site the APPLICATION renderer produces serves ONE document whose head says "Generated application" to anything that does not execute JavaScript. The static/content renderer does it correctly per page via recipes/seo/renderers/static-content/files/src/features/seo/Head.astro, so the two renderers diverge sharply and nothing measured it until now. This is a real product defect, not a scanner artefact: the scanner reports document-title-placeholder, document-description-missing and route-metadata-not-crawlable against it. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately - measuring and changing what a renderer emits are separate changes with separate evidence. The smallest honest fix is generation-time head substitution so the served document at least names the business; full per-route crawlability needs prerendering, which is an architecture decision rather than a patch. Note the mechanism that hid it: the generator copies template files verbatim and substitutes only under src/generated, so index.html has never been project-specific.

gates-evidence-never-runs-in-automation: MEASURED 2026-08-28 and still open, with the cost question answered and the design question not. `npm run gates:evidence` costs 19.8 seconds wall clock and 542MB peak on a warm npm cache, end to end - service replay, generate, install, build, eight producers, npm audit and convergence. Cost is therefore NOT the reason it does not run in CI, and the earlier assumption that it was expensive is wrong. What stops a naive integration is that the command EXITS ZERO while gates fail: on the 2026-08-28 run, seo and performance both FAIL on the nbm build and the process still returns 0, because its only non-zero conditions are `convergence claimed success` and `no gate had every check answered`. Appending it to a workflow as-is would add a permanently green step over two failing gates, which is a vacuous gate and worse than no gate. The defensible first integration is an expectation file: commit the current resolution - which gates are measured, which fail and why - and fail the job on DRIFT from it, so a producer that stops answering or a check that newly fails is caught while the known-unpaid gates stay declared rather than suppressed. Not implemented in this session. What the measurement also produced is a real product finding worth keeping: the seo gate FAILS on the nbm static build with document-description-missing, document-heading-missing and TWO document-description-duplicated findings - three routes share the manifest primaryGoal as their description and two share a registry sentence - so per-route descriptions are being derived from project-level copy where a page has none of its own. That is a static-renderer content defect, separate from the application-renderer metadata work, and it is now measured rather than suspected. Original finding, kept: recorded because it bounds what every gate-producer claim in this repository is worth. `npm run gates:evidence` is the only command that resolves real producer artifacts into gate results through packages/control-plane/src/gate-evidence.js, and it appears in NO GitHub workflow. The resolver and each producer have unit tests; the end-to-end path from a real build to a resolved gate does not run anywhere on a schedule or on a pull request. That is a pre-existing gap rather than a new one, and it means 'this check has a producer' currently means 'a producer exists and is unit-tested', not 'a gate was measured on a build in CI'. Decide deliberately whether to run it in CI - it installs and builds a generated repository, so it is not free - or to record that gate resolution is a local/manual act.
nextStage: Phase 4.5 and beyond are not scheduled here. Within Phase 4.4 the order that survives the 2026-08-28 measurement is: a tenant-scoped records capability first, because it is the one thing standing between the proven tenancy primitives and a coherent application journey; then transactional email, which is the first genuinely missing provider primitive and whose stable contract must describe use case, recipient source, template/event identity, environment, provider connection REFERENCE, delivery result and sandbox behaviour without a provider key ever entering a Build Contract; then uploads/notifications/webhooks/jobs as real consumers appear. Billing last, and only once environment identity, secret references, webhook reconciliation, durable application state, sandbox identity and failure-state testing all exist - it carries production risk that none of the earlier primitives do and must not be pulled forward to make a stage look advanced. The product-proof corpus in docs/GENUINE_BUSINESS_ACCEPTANCE.md continues BESIDE these stages rather than gating them.
recentlyCompleted: Phase 4D presentation invariants and the first genuinely new direction. Two vacuous consumers closed with planted negatives: a distinctive moment that rendered as a corner glyph on the variant richer content earned, and three diversity-counted axes that reached the stylesheet in no form at all. A fourth independent review over three candidates from one frozen pack produced the best result recorded, 6.55, and identified the remaining ceiling as the component vocabulary rather than the art direction. Mobile navigation no longer clips any destination at 390px; schedule rows stack rather than setting descriptions one word per line

Phase 4D source-backed rerun - the decisive experiment. replayIntakeBundle can now carry a frozen approved knowledge pack and the candidate lane passes one, so composition is no longer starved: services went from four bare manifest names rendered as a list to four source-backed entries with descriptions and entity ids rendered as cards, contact gained info@nbm.bz so all three declared conversion goals resolve, and warnings fell from three to one. The one that survives, no-publishable-imagery, is the part of the nbm ceiling that is genuinely the source pack. A guard now refuses to mint candidate evidence when a manifest declares approved sources and the composition is still knowledge-pack-not-provided. 42 captures, 42 distinct content hashes, 6 routes x 3 viewports per candidate, launch readiness launchable with 0 blockers and 6 predicted edits all in imagery, hard constraints 1 enforced 3 routed 0 unclassified, accessibility 6/6 with no serious or critical WCAG A/AA violations

declared-requirement consumers - conversion goals and hard constraints. primaryAction() collapsed call, email and contact form into one Call button on every route; conversionPlan() now resolves every declared goal and places channels by context, and nbm ships two channels plus a recorded gap where its sources hold no email address. manifest.constraints.hard had no reader at all and now has a coverage ledger that reports what enforces each constraint - 1 enforced, 3 routed to the producer that owns the evidence, 0 unclassified on nbm

nbm rerun on the fixed factory - 2 candidates, diversity distinct, 21 captures each with 21 distinct content hashes, DesignLint clean, route identity intact at desktop/tablet/mobile. The #163 capture fix and the #165 responsive fixes both survive a build that was not the one they were written against

first independent Phase 4D visual verdict — an OpenAI GPT-5 design-critic reviewed the nbm candidate set an Anthropic runtime created, and rejected both. The quality system worked: it found a defect the creator had missed and nothing was promoted

route-capture root cause — the evidence server answered every prerendered route with the home document, because it served a path only when that path was itself a file and a prerendered build answers /services with services/index.html. Six routes per viewport were photographed as one page. Reproduced against the frozen nbm inputs, fixed in document resolution rather than by a per-project special case, and proved by six distinct captures whose rendered page identity matches the route requested

4.2A implementation — static/content renderer; deterministic fail-closed renderer selection, six route documents and zero client JavaScript for the business the application renderer serves with one. Its independent visual review is outstanding above, so the stage is not closed
cross-browser visual portability lane; found and fixed a real defect on its first hosted run — the site header was not sticky on any phone
cross-build anti-template diagnostic; advisory by declaration, and it reports the cause of its own findings
controlled bespoke-presentation lane; project-local, token-only, section-scoped, durable across a rebuild and re-validated against the build it lands in

deferredCapabilities.title: Visual excellence — direction, distinctiveness and candidate promotion
deferredCapabilities.reason: MEASURED AND FAILED, not unbuilt. Four independent GPT-5 design-critic reviews over the one frozen genuine business produced a best mean of 6.55 against a required 8.5, and the machinery they measured is complete: directions compile, art-direction axes reach the stylesheet, a distinctive moment holds across every variant its section can take, and candidates compose from the business's own approved sources. What did not move is distinctiveness, which scored between 4.3 and 4.8 on every candidate in every review since v2, through a content fix, a moment/variant contract, an axis-rendering fix and an entirely new direction. The finding that explains it is architectural: the Presentation Registry is the ceiling, because art direction owns token values and section presentations and does not own the component vocabulary, so every candidate inherits the same button treatment, the same CTA grammar, the same display typeface and the same primitive set. The fix is to let a direction select component implementations, which is a design-system change that needs corpus and application evidence to design well and would be badly designed from one thinly-evidenced professional-services business. Continuing to iterate CSS against the same vocabulary was returning less each round. It is deferred so that unrelated website, application, environment, runtime and deterministic-quality work can proceed; it is NOT passed, NOT waived, and its threshold is unchanged.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: Any one of four conditions, and not merely because another CSS adjustment might add 0.3 points. (A) CORPUS: several materially different real projects show whether component-vocabulary convergence is cross-project rather than an artefact of nbm. (B) ARCHITECTURE EARNS IT: a later capability requires art direction or DesignSystemSpec to select project-specific component implementations rather than restyle one set - existing-design-system assimilation (docs/PLATFORM_PARITY_PROGRAMME.md §5.2) is the most likely trigger, because an adopted product arrives with a vocabulary the factory did not choose. (C) PRE-RELEASE QUALIFICATION, MANDATORY: before App Builder claims best-in-class visual output, professional visual maturity or fully proven website generation, this gate must be revisited and paid - the claim may not be made over a deferred gate. (D) A genuinely new benchmark or design evidence materially changes what can be tested.

unpaidGate.finding: The Presentation Registry is the visual ceiling: art direction controls tokens and section presentations but not the component vocabulary, so structurally different directions still draw the same buttons, CTA grammar, dividers and display typeface.

deferredCapabilities.title: Static/content renderer — independent visual parity
deferredCapabilities.reason: MEASURED AND FAILED, with a sequencing dependency that must travel with the number. The independent review scored the static rendering of nbm at mean 5.38 and floor 2.0, against 6.05, 5.74 and 6.55 for the application-rendered candidates reviewed in the same session, so the static rendering is not at least as good and 4.2A does not close. Its distinctiveness 3.0 and distinctive-moment 2.0 are the lowest recorded anywhere in the repository, and the cause is sequencing rather than the renderer: no candidate has ever been promoted, so the static build renders the DEFAULT PRESENTATION SHELL rather than a promoted visual direction. This verdict measures the static renderer carrying the default shell and cannot be read as measuring it carrying an approved direction. What is genuinely proven and not in dispute is real engineering evidence - zero client JavaScript, six route documents, deterministic byte-stable generation and fail-closed renderer selection. Only the visual parity is unpaid, and that debt belongs with the visual-system revisit rather than with the renderer, which is why it does not block application or runtime work.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A visual direction has actually been promoted, at which point the static renderer must be reviewed again carrying that direction rather than the default shell. That makes this dependent on stage 4D's own revival. A renderer-specific correctness defect found independently of the visual system does NOT wait for this and should be fixed when found.

unpaidGate.finding: Not at least as good as the application-rendered candidates, but measured against the default presentation shell because no direction has been promoted for it to present by.

deferredCapabilities.title: Deterministic design-intelligence catalogue
deferredCapabilities.reason: No component asks "which reviewed design patterns fit this project?". BrandSpec reads the knowledge pack's own brand observations, ArtDirectionPlan reads config/layout-patterns.json, and the Presentation Registry is compiled from what the template renders. A catalogue built now would have one producer and no reader.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A real 4D consumer cannot answer a project/industry/intent pattern question from deterministic config. Then document that consumer first, and implement only the smallest lexical (BM25/keyword) catalogue it needs — no vector store, no embeddings, no generic design corpus.

deferredCapabilities.title: MessagingPlan
deferredCapabilities.reason: The composition already carries what a MessagingPlan would organise, with provenance. Page narrative is the section sequence; CTA strategy is derived from the declared conversion goals; proof requirements and their gaps are `declaredProofGap`; audience is on the manifest; forbidden claims are the existing source/provenance boundary. A second narrative authority would have fields nothing reads and a second place the same decision could be made.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: An art-direction or composition decision needs narrative information the composition cannot express — a proof sequence that does not follow from what is available, or an objection-handling order. Implement only the fields that decision reads.

deferredCapabilities.title: Visual comparison canvas
deferredCapabilities.reason: The ordinary Builder Console does the comparison: its candidate panel shows every candidate side by side, switches route and viewport over the captured evidence, names the axes that actually differ, shows the responsive plan and every DesignLint finding, exposes the scoped critic criteria, and promotes exactly one. The single usability failure found was the 330px activity sidebar cropping two full-page captures into roughly 150px columns; moving the panel to the builder stage fixed it. The failing surface was the narrow column, not the Console, so a canvas dependency would be bought against a layout problem.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A concrete comparison task proves the Console cannot do it — spatial arrangement of many more candidates, or freehand annotation a reviewer genuinely needs to hand back. Record the task first.

deferredCapabilities.title: Static semantic icons, Pagefind search, richer typed structured data, deterministic OG imagery
deferredCapabilities.reason: Each needs a real consumer first. The structured data the static renderer emits today is exactly what the factory already supported — a WebSite object, emitted only when the site's own URL is known — because inventing typed entities from facts nothing supports would be a fabricated observation.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A corpus project needs one of them and the absence is a recorded defect rather than a missing feature on a list. Implement only the one that project needed.

deferredCapabilities.title: CMS and content collections
deferredCapabilities.reason: GENUINELY UNBUILT, and not started rather than half-built. What exists is a questionnaire that asks about content; there is no content model, no collection schema, no editing surface and no renderer support. It is deferred rather than implemented because no project in this repository needs it: the one genuine business is a marketing site whose content is frozen approved source, and the application work Phase 4.4 opens on is stateful product data rather than editorial content. Building it now would produce a capability with no consumer, which is the mistake this file already records three times.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A real project needs editorial content that its owner will change after handover, and the absence is a recorded defect on that project rather than a missing row on a list. Implement the content model that project needs and nothing more.

deferredCapabilities.title: Localisation
deferredCapabilities.reason: GENUINELY UNBUILT. One field exists - nfr.localisation.locales in schemas/non-functional-requirements.schema.json - and nothing reads it. No renderer emits a locale, no composition carries translated copy, no route strategy exists and the application document deliberately withholds og:locale rather than asserting one. A single unread schema field is not a partial implementation; it is a field nothing reads.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A real project has a second language its owner actually publishes in. Note that this is also the point at which the withheld og:locale and the html lang attribute stop being defensible defaults and become decisions.

deferredCapabilities.title: Design / Figma import
deferredCapabilities.reason: GENUINELY UNBUILT, of any kind. There is no importer, no token mapping and no component correspondence. It is worth separating from the visual-system debt it looks adjacent to: Phase 4D failed on the component VOCABULARY being fixed across directions, and importing a Figma file would not change that - it would supply values into the same registry that is already the ceiling.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: Either an owner supplies a real design file as the source of truth for a real project, or the existing-design-system assimilation work in docs/PLATFORM_PARITY_PROGRAMME.md §5.2 needs it as an input path. §5.2 is the likelier trigger, and the brownfield profiler is its first half.

deferredCapabilities.title: Brownfield mutation and diagnosis
deferredCapabilities.reason: NOT ATTEMPTED, and deliberately so. The read-only profiler is proven on a real mature repository with zero mutations, and that is the whole of what has been earned. Nothing yet classifies a finding as keep/refactor/redesign/replace/remove/add, nothing reads a deployed URL, nothing executes a project script, and no design system is assimilated. The profiler records all four in its own notAttempted field rather than leaving a reader to infer the boundary from silence. Mutation must not begin because a read succeeded: a baseline of shape counts can notice that a route location disappeared and cannot notice that a route still exists and now returns the wrong thing, and protecting behaviour needs executable and rendered evidence bound to the frozen revision, which a read-only pass does not produce.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: Behavioural evidence exists for an adopted repository at its baseline revision - its own tests observed passing, and rendered evidence captured against its built artifact - so that a change can be shown not to have broken what was working. Diagnosis comes before mutation, and evidence comes before diagnosis.
